· goal: use current stability to address structural vulnerabilities before conditions change.
A neutral figure is being pressured by both The Free Alliance and The Establishment to take a side before the next council session.
The Free Alliance × The Establishment · succession to a council seat · stakes: political influence
road · Picked from pool: road, road, road, isolated, isolated.
mountain_timber · present but depleted (Tier-weighted depletion (20%) marked this resource as depleted.)

The road made Cnocby by a coin’s width, three chances of it against two of nothing, and the mountain timber that raised the travelers’ inn is mostly cut out. What remains worth holding is the seat: the Free Alliance and the Establishment both want the council chair, and both are leaning on the same neutral name to declare before the session. Rónnat Sullivan is about to call something in, and half the inn seems to know what. The mayor wants the cracks mended while the weather holds; no one asks which cracks he means.

The twelve deities of the core pantheon, as a surveyor records them: the name a town swears by, the portfolio it prays over, and the temper the clergy will admit to.
The sea, safe harbour, and the toll of drowning
Smithing, honest weights, and the guild oath
Roads, thresholds, and the traveller’s luck
Harvest, stored grain, and the lean winter

On the coast road; a tidal harbour
A wall town that learned to trade with the sea it once feared.

You come to Thornwall by the coast road, and the wall shows first: grey stone the height of four men, salt-stained on its seaward face. The gate stands open in daylight; a toll-clerk keeps a ledger you are welcome to read and unwelcome to argue with. Beyond, the town falls toward a tidal harbour where the fishing fleet lies careened at low water and the warehouses smell of pitch and drying cod.
A merchant council, lately at odds with the harbour guild.
Salt, salt-cod, and the toll on the coast road.
The wall is sound; the garrison is thin and underpaid.
A winter of storms has pushed the bar across the harbour mouth; deep-keeled ships now wait for the tide or unload offshore.
The council will pay well for a survey of the bar, and better for anyone who can move it.
Reads every ledger; trusts none of them.
Buried three husbands to the tide; blesses the fleet anyway.
Would rather dredge than be dredged out of business.
The toll-clerk’s ledger shows a barge that pays the road toll but is never seen on the road.
Mother Vane wants the old sea-shrine on the bar re-consecrated before the dredging disturbs it.
A Redwater factor is quietly buying up silted-harbour warehouses at a loss, or an investment.

How goods, news, and trouble move through the settlement. Crossroads = high diversity. River = food security. Isolated = thin services, high secrets.
Constrains what the settlement can produce, defend, and rely on. Coastal towns import grain; mountain holds export stone. Frontier terrains bias toward militarized institutions.

Names, naming patterns, institution flavor, faction archetypes. Drives the prose of the place more than the math. A "germanic" town and a "south-asian" town with identical configs read very differently.
Heartland = monsters are rumor. Frontier = active patrols. Plagued = the militia is the most important institution and people lock their doors at dusk.
None = magic is disabled. Low = rare and limited. Medium = a moderate, everyday presence. High = broad and pervasive. The level shapes institution distribution and NPC archetypes.

{settlement} is bound to terms it took against every grudge it holds, and the hall carried them; nobody here likes the arrangement, and nobody here proposes undoing it.
The seat's revenue at {settlement} is up and its standing among the neighbouring halls is down, and the tithe contest it won against {temple} is the one entry both movements hang from.

The old factors can name the week the renewals stopped, and will point out that every refusal was its own reasonable page and every one of them is still in the book.
The trade in {good} has not come back to {settlement} with the truth: the counters that refused are refusing yet, and being right about it is no longer the question.
{house}'s counters at {settlement} are open and its books are thick: the story reached here at the fourth hand and stopped, no counter refused, and the market carries no mark of it at all.
The obligations in {settlement}'s book run to households at {counterpart}, generation upon generation of them, and the silver that raised these walls came down that column.
Half the roofs of {settlement} were paid for out of {counterpart}, and the people under them will tell you their grandfathers left in a bad season and named where they were going as they went.
{settlement} is new work standing on old foundations, raised again by the descendants of the people who emptied it.
The memory was written at both ends and has not finished decaying at {counterpart}; the elders of {settlement} count that, and not the harvest, as the reason there was money at all.
A claim stands filed out of {settlement}, sworn on a memory {timeband_age} and priced no differently for its age: the grudge came home with the silver and is entered beside it.
The old site of {settlement} is a ruin still: the households at {counterpart} took up the host's rites and stopped entering it as home, and the funding stopped when the entering did.
{temple}'s new chapter stands on credit and the credit came out of the hungry season here; there is no gift anywhere in the house's book, which is what makes the entry legible.
The town has worked out whose money seated its minister, and the anger has gone to the altar rather than to the merchant.
The chapter house is the newest building in {settlement} and the one people here are least willing to discuss.
Those who queued that winter remember who was selling into the gap, and remember that {house} keeps its books a town over at {counterpart}, where nobody from {settlement} can read them.
{timeband_since}, {temple} is still answering for the provenance, and every reading out of that pulpit is weighed against a ledger before it is weighed against anything else.
{temple}'s chapter owes nobody and carries no stain: the credit was refused at the door on the same provenance the stain would have ridden, and the corner still happened here regardless.
The war {settlement} fought over a creek nobody at its court had seen is closed, and its own opening receipt names a misjudgment as the deciding term; no clerk has softened it since.

The old hands say the creek grew in every mouth it passed through, and they are right. The record keeps the drift relay by relay, which is rarer than being right.
The arrivals who were turned back are counted home again and {settlement} carries the crowding of the ones who landed; {timeband_since} the roll is still settling.
{settlement} is at peace and no clerk had to soften the reason: the letters home corrected the belief, the reckonings ground together, and the receipt names which of the two closed the war.

The channel {faction} trusts at {settlement} is {house}'s and was theirs before the errand was: {npc} carries the cargo off the {route} road to {house} first and to {counterpart} after, and the divergence sits exactly where the detour is.
Nothing written stands between {settlement} and {counterpart}: the {term} reached its date and the clerks struck it, and the book is the only place it was mourned.

Nobody at {settlement} calls it a breach and nobody ever had to: the wagons came a little short and then a little shorter, through {timeband_span}, and the clerks weighed what arrived against what was promised until the ledger would not close.

The {term} is {timeband_age} and no hand that signed it still holds a seat; the market cannot name one of them.

There is nothing left to renew and nobody moving to renew it: the window opened, the chancery let the season pass, and the clerks entered that as a decision because there was nothing else to enter it as.

The {term} between {settlement} and {counterpart} still stands, re-cut rather than let go: a mediator sat the two courts down over a pact neither had broken, and the terms {settlement} argued itself hoarse over are the ones it keeps.
Every term under the treaty with {counterpart} is defaulted from the week {npc} said so, and the parchment is kept at {settlement} only as evidence.
The town remarks that nothing was seized and nothing was burned: the renunciation was read out in the square, and the clerks defaulted the {term} before the square had emptied.
Courts have begun pricing what a promise out of {settlement} is worth, and they are pricing it low.
This house has disavowed {band} times before, and the entry has sat {timeband_since} in every chancery that keeps such entries.
The next proposal out of {settlement} will be refused on the credibility rather than on the terms, and there will be no arguing it, because there are no terms to argue.

The treaty with {counterpart} stands, and stands because nobody spoke: no word came from the new seat there and the date passed, which is what the law reads silence as, and {settlement}'s captains declined to believe it for as long as they were able.
{settlement}'s book carries two columns and joins neither: the instalments to {counterpart} left on time, every time, and the standing of the seat that sent them fell over the very same seasons.

{burden} stands on {settlement} and the standing of the seat that pays has fallen over the same seasons, and it is the hall that has joined the two: the book carries the columns and no line between them, and the book is what was read out at the verdict.
A stranger at {settlement} will hear several accounts of what the town pays {counterpart} and no two alike; the terms are sealed, and the town has filled the gap with its own arithmetic.
The older hands hold that the bill was another court's and say so without expecting to be believed: {npc} paid what a treaty required {settlement} to pay, and it cost {npc} the seat.

The hall at {settlement} has been quiet for as long as the muster has been full, and the quiet is not agreement; the men who would have carried a motion against the seat are carrying spears, and nobody has had to find out yet what they would have said.
Here the fall has a named cause and the clerks can point to the week: the seat lost standing for {reason}, exposed and entered, and the tribute and the war stood exactly where they had stood.

The rows against {counterpart} are in {settlement}'s book and are not counted when the hall counts {counterpart}: the war party can read them and cannot cite them, and the standing grievance reads {band} lighter for it.
The town has never stopped arguing about which cost more, the grain or the pride: the price was read out in the square before witnesses who will outlive the seat that swore it.
{settlement} will tell you the quarrel is buried. {counterpart} has buried nothing, and a decree binds only the hall that made it.
{faction} has waited in the open since the decree was read, and the elders here know the difference between a grudge that is closed and one that is merely uncited.
A later hall at {counterpart} cited the rows anyway, word for word, and {timeband_since} the old {wound} is back in {settlement}'s book with a new one on top of it for the revoking.

{counterpart} keeps its quarrel and {settlement} keeps the receipt: the price was paid in full against the wrong account (the carts went and were taken and thanked for), and the {temple} that witnessed the swearing has been asked about it twice since.
DS-DEF-1: `Defense › Defensive posture header` · `defenseProfile.readiness + resourceAnalysis.{terrain,strategicValue} + safetyProfile.guardEffectivenessDesc`
{settlement} reads as a defended place from the road in: the approaches are watched, the works are kept up, and none of it looks like it was thrown together.
What {settlement} can field and what {settlement} has built are both in good order; the town would take real effort to threaten and knows it.
The town does not spend much time thinking about being attacked, and the reason is not complacency. The arrangements are in place, and the town is not relying on anything else instead.
Nothing presses {settlement} at present, and the absence is not luck: a town this well set is not worth the price of trying.
{settlement} is covered against what it is likely to face, with little left over. The arrangements work and would not survive being tested twice at once.
A stranger sees an ordinary defended town at {settlement}: enough on the walls to be serious, not enough to be reassuring.
The town believes it could hold against the usual trouble and does not claim more than that, which is a fair reading of what it has.
{settlement} is at the point where the arrangements are sufficient and nothing is spare. One more demand on them and the town would be choosing which pressure to leave uncovered.
The defensive arrangements at {settlement} are thin. Something is in place against most pressures and nothing is in place in depth.
What a stranger notices at {settlement} is how much of the perimeter has nobody on it, and how normal the town seems to find that.
{settlement} is getting by on not being tested. The margin has been narrowing rather than widening, and nothing in hand is closing it.
{settlement} is effectively undefended. There is no arrangement here that would slow a serious attempt on the town by more than the time it takes to walk in.
The town knows perfectly well what it could not survive, and the knowledge shapes what it will and will not provoke.
A stranger reaches the centre of {settlement} without being stopped, challenged or counted by anybody at all.
The ground does more for {settlement} than the town does. The approach is narrow, and anything coming at it has to come the long way and in the open.
{settlement} is sited where the terrain carries part of the defense; what the town has built is worth more here than the same works would be on flat ground.
The ground here does the arguing. Anything weighing an attempt on {settlement} has to weigh the approach first, and the approach is the part that does not improve with numbers.
{settlement} sits open. There is no ground here that helps it, and everything the town has must be built rather than found.
The site gives {settlement} nothing defensively. Every advantage the town holds is one it has paid for and must keep paying for.
The town has no hill and no narrows and does not pretend otherwise; what {settlement} holds it holds by standing on it.
{settlement} holds something worth taking, and that is the whole of the defensive problem: the town must be worth more to keep than it is to seize.
The town is aware of what it sits on and aware that others are aware, and the awareness runs underneath a great deal of what it decides.
A stranger understands within a day why anybody would want {settlement}, and understands shortly afterwards why the town is so careful about who it offends.
Nothing at {settlement} is worth an army's season, and the town's best defense is that plain fact rather than anything on its walls.
{settlement} is not a prize. What it can field matters less here than what it does not have that anyone would come for.
The town knows it is not worth taking and has made a kind of peace with the knowledge, which is not the same as being comfortable with it.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: plagued, perimeter AND organized force[0].text
text: The country around {settlement} is thick with creatures and the town has answered it properly: there is a wall to hold and there are people to hold it, and both are in use constantly.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: plagued, perimeter AND organized force[1].text
text: Defense at {settlement} is not an emergency arrangement, it is the week's work: the rotations run, the gates close on time, and nobody treats any of it as unusual.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: plagued, perimeter AND organized force[2].text
text: What {settlement} has built is holding against the pressure and is being spent doing it; the posture is survivable, and survivable is the most that can be said of it here.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: plagued, perimeter but NO force to hold it[0].text
text: {settlement} has a wall and nobody to man it. The line is a chokepoint on paper and a chokepoint requires people standing in it, which this town cannot supply for more than a night.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: plagued, perimeter but NO force to hold it[1].text
text: A stranger walks the perimeter at {settlement} and finds long stretches of good work with nobody on them, in a country where that matters a great deal.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: plagued, perimeter but NO force to hold it[2].text
text: The works at {settlement} are doing less each season as the watch thins, and the thinning is not being reversed.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: plagued, NO perimeter and NO force[0].text
text: An embattled country and nothing organized standing in it: {settlement} has no line, no force and no specialist recourse, and survival here rests on terrain, distance and the ability to leave.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: plagued, NO perimeter and NO force[1].text
text: The town does not defend itself. What it does is watch, and move, and hope the pressure goes around it, and that is understood by everyone in it.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: plagued, NO perimeter and NO force[2].text
text: A stranger arriving at {settlement} understands the danger before anybody explains it, because nothing about the place is arranged as though danger were expected to be met.
{settlement} sits on an active frontier with a line and a force behind it. Most of what comes out of the country will not press a defended perimeter, and most of what comes here does not.
The town takes the frontier seriously and has taken it seriously long enough that the arrangements are ordinary rather than anxious.
Very little reaches {settlement} out of the wild country, and the reason is that the arrangements are visible from a long way off.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: frontier, force without a perimeter[0].text
text: {settlement} keeps armed people on an open frontier, which means the defense is reactive: whatever comes chooses where the fighting happens, and the town arrives afterwards.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: frontier, force without a perimeter[1].text
text: A stranger finds soldiers at {settlement} and no wall for them to stand on, and can see how that would go against anything that arrived in more than one place.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: frontier, force without a perimeter[2].text
text: The town can answer trouble and cannot prevent it, and the difference costs it something every season.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: settled, defenses beyond the need[0].angle
DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: settled, defenses beyond the need[0].text
text: There is very little in the country around {settlement} and there are substantial works facing it; whatever the walls here are for, it is not the creatures.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: settled, defenses beyond the need[1].text
text: {settlement} is comfortably over-provided against beasts. The pressures that matter to this town are internal, and its defensive spending does not reflect that.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Beasts & Monsters: settled, defenses beyond the need[2].text
text: A stranger notices the perimeter at {settlement} chiefly for how relaxed the people on it are.
{settlement} keeps no organized defense against the country, and in a heartland this quiet the arrangement is a reasonable one rather than a gap.
The town has never needed to think about what is outside it, and does not.
A stranger walks out of {settlement} in any direction at any hour and meets nothing that would justify a watch.
{settlement} has a line and professionals to hold it, which is real deterrence against raiding and against a conventional assault; it is not a posture rated for a long siege without stores behind it.
A stranger sizing {settlement} up sees the two things that matter together (the wall and the men who belong to it) and revises what an attempt would cost.
The town believes it could be held, and the belief is founded on something rather than on hope.
Walls at {settlement} with townspeople behind them: credible against raiders, and inadequate against anybody who arrives professionally and brought siege gear.
The town would turn out and does not pretend that turning out is the same as being defended.
What {settlement} has would hold against the first thing and is unlikely to hold against the second, and nothing in hand changes that.
{settlement} has walls and nobody to put on them. A determined attacker takes this town with ladders and patience, and requires nothing else.
A stranger at {settlement} sees a serious perimeter and a serious absence of anyone standing in it.
The town has the thing that would save it and not the people who would use it, and says so when pressed.
{settlement} keeps a professional force and no perimeter. It answers raiders well and cannot hold a siege, because there is nothing here to hold.
The town's defense is people rather than works, and people can be gone around.
A stranger sees soldiers at {settlement} and no line for them to stand behind, and can see how that decides where any fight would happen.
{settlement} can put armed citizens on their own ground, which counts for something against a disorganized raid and for nothing at all against a disciplined force.
The town knows its own country and knows that knowing it is not an answer to a professional army.
A stranger at {settlement} meets armed townspeople who are entirely competent on their own ground and have never stood in a line with anybody.
{settlement} has no line and no force. Organized aggression cannot be resisted here; what preserves the town is distance, diplomacy, or being beneath notice.
Nothing has come for {settlement} and nothing about the town would stop it. The safety here is entirely a matter of nobody having wanted to.
The town's plan for an army is to not be interesting to one, and everybody here can state the plan.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Internal Security: full legal chain (court AND prison)[0].text
text: {settlement} can arrest, try and hold, and having all three means the town's law is a process rather than a threat.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Internal Security: full legal chain (court AND prison)[1].text
text: A thing done wrong at {settlement} goes somewhere and takes time, and the town has come to rely on that rather than on the watch's temper.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Internal Security: full legal chain (court AND prison)[2].text
text: A stranger who brings a complaint at {settlement} is given a procedure rather than a favour, and the procedure runs.
{settlement} tries offences it cannot hold anyone for; the sentences available here are money and exile, and both of them fall unevenly.
The town's law can name a wrong and cannot keep the person who did it, so it reaches for the purse or the road.
Each judgment {settlement} cannot enforce costs the next one a little of its weight, and the town's courts are spending down a reputation they cannot replace.
{settlement} can hold people and has no settled way of deciding whether it should, which makes enforcement here a matter of who is doing it.
A stranger at {settlement} is careful in a way he would not need to be in a town with courts, and cannot say precisely why.
The town can put a person away at {settlement} and cannot say on what grounds, and has learned not to ask on whose.
There is no legal machinery at {settlement}; order here rests on force alone, and force alone deters only while it is present.
The town settles things itself, quickly, and does not always settle them well.
A stranger wronged at {settlement} discovers there is nowhere to take it, and that the discovery surprises nobody local.
{settlement} can absorb a sustained crisis out of its own revenue: emergency measures can be paid for and the garrison can be kept paid while they last.
The town could go through a bad season with its arrangements intact, and the people who would have to be paid through one know it.
Trouble at {settlement} has not turned into a collapse, and the reason is money. A town that can pay through a crisis mostly does.
{settlement} can fund a short crisis. A long one begins eating reserves within a few months, and the reserves are not deep enough to hide that from anybody.
The town's capacity to pay for its own emergencies is real and finite, and every season of pressure moves the finite part closer.
{settlement} can pay for a crisis of the ordinary length; the edge of what it can fund lies a few months past the beginning of one, and the town has not been asked to find out where.
Chronic shortfall at {settlement} limits what the town can do in an emergency before the emergency starts; the pay is irregular, and irregular pay shows up as morale exactly when it matters.
The people who would have to hold {settlement} through something are already owed, and they have not forgotten it.
The shortfall at {settlement} is chronic rather than sudden, and each season of it removes a little more of what the town could do about a crisis when one comes.
{settlement} cannot fund a response to anything. Any sustained pressure exhausts the town's capacity almost immediately and then continues.
The town is not spending its way out of trouble because there is nothing to spend, and each thing that goes wrong makes the next thing cheaper to happen.
The town could not pay for a bad month at {settlement}, and the people who would have to be paid know it.
{settlement} holds food against a bad year and has somewhere to put the sick; between them the town can take a failed harvest or an outbreak without either becoming a catastrophe.
The town has a place for grain and a place for the ill, and knows exactly what having both is worth.
Neither a failed harvest nor an outbreak turns into a catastrophe at {settlement}, and the reason is in the two buildings rather than in the luck.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Disasters & Famine: granary AND parish care only[0].text
text: There is food stored at {settlement} and there are clergy who tend the sick: reserves against hunger, and against disease something better than nothing and well short of a hospital.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Disasters & Famine: granary AND parish care only[1].text
text: The town can eat through a bad year. What it does about a plague is pray and nurse, in that order.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Disasters & Famine: granary AND parish care only[2].text
text: A stranger finds a full store and a modest infirmary at {settlement}, and can see which of the two the town has spent its thinking on.
{settlement} can feed itself through a failed harvest and has nothing at all against disease; a sickness here spreads until it stops of its own accord.
The stores will carry the town through hunger. Nothing here will carry it through a plague, and the town has not built anything that would.
The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one, and knows which of the two it fears.
{settlement} can treat and contain an outbreak and keeps no food against a bad harvest; a crop failure here becomes hardship the same season it happens.
The town is better prepared for the sickness than for the hunger, which is an unusual way round and does not comfort anyone.
{settlement} is arranged against the sickness it has seen and not against the hunger it has not, and nothing in hand is correcting the imbalance.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Disasters & Famine: NO reserves, NO medical provision[0].text
text: {settlement} holds no food against a bad year and has nobody to treat the sick; a failed harvest is immediate hardship here and a plague runs until it burns out.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Disasters & Famine: NO reserves, NO medical provision[1].text
text: The town's answer to a bad season is the same as its answer to a sickness, which is to endure it and count afterwards.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-2.pools.Disasters & Famine: NO reserves, NO medical provision[2].text
text: A stranger looking for the granary or the sick-house at {settlement} is directed to neither, because there is neither.
Nothing much happens to people at {settlement}. The watch is heavier than anything working against it, by a margin the town does not have to think about.
A stranger walks {settlement} at any hour without being troubled, and notices that the locals do the same without appearing to have decided to.
Enforcement at {settlement} sits far above whatever criminal presence the town holds; the returns are thin because there is very little to return.
There is money at {settlement} and there is opportunity, and neither has produced an organized interest. The watch here is simply too heavy to be worth the arrangement.
{settlement} is a quiet town. Things are taken occasionally and the taking does not spread, because the people who would spread it are known.
Enforcement at {settlement} is clearly the stronger side; criminal work here is suppressed rather than absent, and stays suppressed.
A stranger is comfortable at {settlement} and is also aware that the comfort has somebody maintaining it.
{settlement} runs on a working balance: the law is present, crime exists, and neither has the run of the town.
Enforcement and criminal presence at {settlement} sit close enough that the town's condition is a matter of which way the next few seasons go.
A stranger at {settlement} is told which streets to avoid and finds the advice specific, short and accurate.
The balance at {settlement} sits where either side could take it. A thinner watch or a bolder operator would show up in the returns within the season, and nothing else would need to change.
Crime at {settlement} is outrunning the watch. It is not chaos; it is that the people doing it have stopped expecting to be caught.
What criminal work is being done at {settlement} measurably exceeds what is being answered, and the gap is legible in the returns rather than merely felt.
The balance at {settlement} has tipped and is still tipping. Each season the watch answers a smaller share of what happens.
The watch at {settlement} has been overwhelmed. What happens in this town is decided by whoever is present when it happens.
Organized interests at {settlement} now outweigh enforcement outright; there is no part of the town's order that does not run through somebody's permission.
A stranger at {settlement} is not warned about particular streets, because the warning would have to cover all of them.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-3.pools.COMPOUND override (a crisis stress has rewritten the label)[0].text
text: The ordinary safety of {settlement} has stopped applying. Whatever the town was, the crisis on it now is what governs the streets.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-3.pools.COMPOUND override (a crisis stress has rewritten the label)[1].text
text: The town's usual reading does not describe {settlement} at present; the standing condition has been overtaken by the crisis and the watch is arranged around that instead.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-3.pools.COMPOUND override (a crisis stress has rewritten the label)[2].text
text: Order at {settlement} is being held under a pressure the town's arrangements were not built for, and how long it holds is a question about the pressure rather than about the watch.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-3.pools.First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)[0].text
text: This is what {settlement} looks like on a first pass; a season here would either confirm it or correct it, and nobody has spent the season yet.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-3.pools.First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)[1].text
text: The safety reading for {settlement} is an initial one. It is honest about what has been seen and says nothing about what has not.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_DEFENSE.DS-DEF-3.pools.First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)[2].text
text: What the town says about its own safety at {settlement} is what the town says on a first acquaintance, and a longer one would be a different account.
DS-DEF-4: `Defense › Criminal structure + capture consequence` · `deriveCriminalStructure(settlement) + powerStructure.criminalCaptureState + safetyProfile.criminalInstitutions[]`
Crime at {settlement} has an order to it. What is permitted is permitted by somebody, random violence is put down because it draws attention, and the arrangement is stable enough to negotiate with.
The criminal interest at {settlement} is a hierarchy rather than a nuisance: predictable, rule-bound, and extracting steadily from the same places every season.
A stranger at {settlement} is not robbed and is quietly told what the arrangement is; the danger here is systematic rather than sudden.
There is very little street violence at {settlement} and it is not the watch's doing. A structured interest suppresses what draws enforcement, and does it more thoroughly than the watch could.
Criminal work at {settlement} is coordinated enough to hold routes and territories and not coordinated enough to have a head; several interests are running, and none of them is the one to talk to.
The town knows there are arrangements at {settlement} and cannot say whose, because the answer changes by street and by season.
What is being contested at {settlement} is who gets to be the arrangement, and until that settles the town gets the cost of both a syndicate and a scramble.
Crime at {settlement} is opportunistic and unorganized: fences, bandits and small operators working for themselves, with nothing to threaten and nobody to buy.
Things go missing at {settlement} and no one profits by it twice; there is no structure here, which makes it less dangerous and much harder to stop.
A stranger at {settlement} is at risk from individuals rather than from an arrangement, which is worse in the moment and better in every other way.
No criminal infrastructure has been identified at {settlement}. Whatever wrongdoing the town has does not run through anything that could be called an organization.
What goes wrong at {settlement} goes wrong one thing at a time and belongs to whoever did it.
A stranger asking after the arrangements at {settlement} is met with genuine incomprehension, which is either the truth or an unusually good performance of it.
Nothing criminal has reached the {seat} at {settlement}. Whatever operates in the town operates outside the hall, and the hall's decisions are the hall's.
There is a criminal interest at {settlement} with the means to reach into the hall and it has not; the seat's people are watched too closely for the approach to be worth its risk.
Whatever is being run at {settlement} is being run outside the hall, and the town's dealings with the hall are the town's dealings with the hall.
The {seat} at {settlement} and the criminal interest here are opposed, actively, and the opposition is the arrangement. Each is spending on the other and neither is winning.
The hall at {settlement} moves against the operators and the operators move back, and the town is where the two of them meet.
The hall and the operators at {settlement} are each spending on the other and neither is gaining, and the spending is coming out of things the town needed.
The {seat} at {settlement} and the criminal interest have found a line and both keep to it; nothing is bought here, and nothing is pressed either.
There is an understanding at {settlement} that nobody has written down: what is permitted, and where the permitting stops.
The balance at {settlement} holds because both sides prefer it, which is a different thing from either side being restrained.
Somebody at the {seat} of {settlement} is carrying a leash, and the decisions that come out of the hall now bend around it in ways the rolls will not show.
The criminal interest at {settlement} has bought into the hall rather than around it, and each decision it shapes makes the next one cheaper to shape.
The town at {settlement} does not know, and is beginning to notice that certain matters never quite conclude.
The {seat} at {settlement} is held. What the hall decides is decided elsewhere and announced here, and the announcing is the only part the town sees.
There is no longer a distinction at {settlement} between the criminal interest and the governing one; the town is being administered by its syndicate through the forms of its hall.
A stranger at {settlement} conducts perfectly ordinary business with the hall and never learns whose business it actually was.
There is a line around {settlement} and it is kept: the gates shut, the works are repaired, and a stranger enters where the town intends him to.
{settlement} controls its own entry points. That is what a perimeter buys: not invulnerability, but the choice of where anything happens.
The town has a wall and arranges its day around the gates without noticing that it does.
{settlement} is unfortified. There is no perimeter, which means the town cannot control entry and cannot make a chokepoint of anything.
A stranger arrives at {settlement} from whichever direction suits him and is not obliged to pass anybody on the way in.
The town has an edge rather than a boundary at {settlement}, and the edge is wherever the last building happens to be.
{settlement} keeps a standing force: people whose work is the defense of this town and who are answerable for it as work.
The soldiers at {settlement} belong to the town rather than to a season; they are a fixture, with all the friction and all the reliability of one.
A stranger at {settlement} is counted at the gate by somebody whose job that is, and is counted again on the way out.
{settlement}'s defense is its own people under arms. They know the ground, they can be raised, and raising them stops everything else the town was doing.
The town turns out when it must and goes back to work after, and understands that this is a different thing from having soldiers.
{settlement} could keep soldiers and does not; the town has decided that arming itself when needed costs less than paying anybody to be armed all year.
{settlement} keeps a watch, which is a matter of order rather than of war. It answers what happens inside the walls and is not built for what arrives outside them.
There are people walking the town at {settlement} at night, and the town's sense of itself rests more on that than on anything at the gate.
A stranger walking {settlement} late is looked at rather than stopped, and the looking is systematic enough to notice.
{settlement} has no organized force. Defense here is individual armed citizens, with no command, no training and no way to coordinate a response.
The town would defend itself as a crowd defends itself, which is to say briefly and in several directions at once.
A stranger at {settlement} can find nobody whose responsibility the town's defense is, because it is not anybody's.
Part of what defends {settlement} is contracted rather than owed: competent, available, and loyal for exactly as long as the terms run.
The town pays for some of its soldiers and knows which ones, and treats them accordingly.
The contracted companies at {settlement} are doing the work they were engaged for, and the engagement has an end written into it that the town has not yet had to think about.
{settlement} keeps a charter for specialist work. The things a garrison is wrong for go to people retained to handle exactly them.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-1.pools.COMBINATION C4: a low rung on a working approach[2].text
text: A stranger arriving by the {access} finds more moving through {settlement} than settling in it. The market turns, and the town does not thicken on the turning.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-1.pools.COMBINATION C5: a low rung on a narrow approach[0].text
text: {settlement} is poor and hard to reach, and the two read as one fact: what the road does not carry, the town does without.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-1.pools.COMBINATION C5: a low rung on a narrow approach[1].text
text: The books are short in the ordinary way: a {complexity} sized to the town and no further, and no approach wide enough to change the arithmetic.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-1.pools.COMBINATION C5: a low rung on a narrow approach[2].text
text: {settlement} is poor and hard to reach, and the two hold each other in place: nothing about the approach would change the arithmetic, and nothing in the arithmetic would pay to widen the approach.
{settlement} does not grow what it eats. The daily count comes up short and the shortfall is made good off the road, week on week, as a standing line in the accounts.
Bread here is bought, not simply had. The fields do not cover the town and everyone knows which day the carts come.
The granary doors open more often than they shut, and what comes out is not what the fields put in.
{settlement} eats well below what it raises. The excess is counted, stored, and argued over rather than needed.
The talk about food here is about price, not about enough. The fields have been good to the town and the stores show it.
A stranger notices the loaded carts leaving {settlement} rather than arriving. What the town grows, the town cannot finish.
What {settlement} raises and what {settlement} eats come out level. There is no shortfall to cover and nothing spare to sell.
Food is not a subject here. The town feeds itself, and it feeds itself exactly.
{settlement} sits level on food. The fields answer the town and no further, so a single failure would be felt at once and a good season would not be noticed.
The granary stands near its capacity going into {season}. The stores reach past the turn of the year with room to spare.
Nobody is counting sacks in {settlement} this {season}. The granary is full and the argument is about the overflow.
The stores here are the reassuring kind: a granary standing deep in {season}, and a town that plainly expects to stay that way.
The granary holds a working reserve into {season}: enough to carry the town through, not enough to lend.
The stores will do. That is the whole of what {settlement} says about its granary this {season}.
The granary is stocked and not deep. It answers {season} as things stand and would not answer {season} plus a failure.
The granary runs thin this {season}. What is left is measured in a stretch of weeks rather than a stretch of seasons, and the measuring is being done.
People in {settlement} have begun asking when the granary was last this low, which is the question that comes before the harder ones.
The stores are drawing down faster than {season} will replace them, and the gap between the two is the town's whole immediate problem.
The granary is very nearly out. What remains is counted daily and issued against a list.
The granary door is watched now. There is little behind it and everybody knows roughly how little.
A stranger who asks about the stores gets a short answer and a changed subject. The granary is all but empty and {season} has not turned.
DS-ECO-3: Economics › Live Trade Flow drift · `spatialLedgers.tradeFlow[sid]{in,out}` + `isTradeDependent(economicState)` → `{throughputBand, dependency, magnitude}`
The roads have gone quiet. Little reaches the markets, and what the town depends on is not arriving.
The gate returns are thin in both columns. What arrives is short of what the town has contracted for, and the shortfall is in goods the town does not make.
Market days are quiet and short. The stalls that depend on the roads are the ones standing empty.
Traffic into {settlement} has fallen below what the town runs on, and the stores are covering the difference for now.
Little moves on {settlement}'s roads and the books barely register it. The town buys and sells almost nothing beyond its own walls.
The roads are quiet. In a town that lives off its own fields, quiet roads are a matter of company rather than supply.
A stranger finds the approaches empty and the market unbothered. The two go together here.
Caravans keep to their rounds. Trade moves at its accustomed pace.
The traffic through {settlement} matches what the ledgers expect of it. Arrivals and departures come out even, week on week.
The carts come when the carts come. Nobody is watching the road for them.
Trade here reads as unremarkable, which on a road is the good reading.
The roads are busy. Caravans arrive thick and depart laden, and the markets are well-fed.
More is moving through {settlement} than the town's own trade accounts for. Everything the market depends on arrives ahead of its need.
The yard is full most mornings and the market is fat on it. What the town cannot make, the town can simply buy.
A stranger will wait behind carts to get in. The roads are working harder than the town requires of them.
Heavy traffic runs through {settlement} without much of it belonging to the town: the roads are busy, the books are local.
Plenty passes here. Not much of it stops.
The traffic on these roads outruns the market. What arrives is mostly going somewhere else.
DS-ECO-4: Economics › Market Prices · `deriveMarketPrices(...)` → `{exports[], imports[], highlight{label,tag,crierLine}}`
{good} is the price everyone here quotes first, and it quotes high. The stores are short of it and the crier's reckoning follows the shortage rather than any rate.
What this market talks about is the cost of {good}. It is dear, it has been dear, and the crier says so before he says anything else.
A stranger's coin goes furthest on everything in {settlement} except {good}, which is scarce enough that the market prices it out loud.
The market is ordinary but for {good}: stocks of it have fallen far enough to move the crier's coarse reckoning, and nothing else has.
{good} sells for little here. The stores are heavy with it and the reckoning has come down to meet the pile.
Anyone selling {good} in {settlement} is selling it badly. There is too much of it and the price says so.
A stranger buying {good} does well in this market. Nothing else is priced kindly.
{good} keeps arriving faster than it leaves, and the price has been giving way to it.
Nothing in {settlement}'s market is priced out of the ordinary. Every good the town trades sits within its accustomed reckoning.
The crier has nothing to make a noise about. Prices here are what prices here usually are.
A stranger will find no bargains and no robberies. The market is level across the board.
No good is scarce enough or heavy enough to move its price, so every stall sits inside its ordinary reckoning, and it would take a real movement in the stores to put any of them outside it.
The two halves of this market disagree. What the town sells is dear and what the town buys is cheap, and both readings come off the same week's stocks.
Sellers here are doing well and so are buyers, which is not the ordinary shape of a market and is the first thing a trader will remark on.
A trader arriving at {settlement} pays dear for what the town makes and gets little for what he brought.
The town's own goods are running short while what it imports keeps piling up, and the crier prices both movements in the same breath.
DS-ECO-5: Economics › Economic Flows chain cards · `economicState.activeChains[]{status, dependency, entrepot, entrepotNote, magicNote, magicRecovery, processingInstitutions[], outputs[]}`
The {chain} is running below what it should. It wants {resource} the town cannot supply, and the shortfall reaches the services that draw on it.
{institution} is still open and still short. What it needs has not been coming, and the work it cannot do is felt further down.
{settlement}'s {chain} produces less with every turn it goes without {resource}, and the trades below it are shortening their own work to match.
The {chain} runs, and it runs on no margin. Every input it needs is arriving and none of it is arriving spare.
The {chain} is intact and exposed at once. It works while everything holds and has nothing behind it if one link gives.
The people working the {chain} are not idle and are not comfortable. One bad month upstream would put them down.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-5.pools.RUNNING (canonical stable): draw only with the note fields empty (R-DST-F)[0].text
text: The {chain} runs whole. {institution} has what it needs, the outputs come off as expected, and nothing in the line is being covered for.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-5.pools.RUNNING (canonical stable): draw only with the note fields empty (R-DST-F)[1].text
text: A stranger watching {settlement}'s {chain} sees the ordinary version of it: {resource} in at one end, {good} out at the other, and no gap between.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-5.pools.RUNNING (canonical stable): draw only with the note fields empty (R-DST-F)[2].text
text: Nobody talks about the {chain}. It works, it has worked, and the town's attention is elsewhere.
{settlement} does not make {good}; it handles it. The goods enter, change hands and leave, and the town's earnings are in the handling.
What passes through here does not stay long enough to be made into anything. The warehouses are full and the workshops are not.
The trade belongs to other places. {settlement}'s part of it is the road, the yard and the cut.
The {chain} is held up by a working rather than by its own supply, and the working covers a corner of what the line needs.
The {chain} is standing on a prop. The prop is real and it is small. Most of what the line lacks, it still lacks.
The {chain} runs on {institution}'s craft and everyone knows the craft is not enough. It buys time; it does not buy supply.
The {chain} runs almost whole on a working. The books show the output nearly where it belongs and the line beneath it replaced rather than repaired.
A stranger would see nothing wrong with this {chain}. What is wrong is that the thing carrying it is a craft and not a road.
The {chain} should have failed and has not. What it lost is being made good by a working strong enough to stand in for nearly all of it.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-5.pools.OPERATIONAL: the service economy (no line of supply behind it)[0].text
text: {institution} sells work rather than goods. There is no line of supply to break. The service stands as long as the house stands.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-5.pools.OPERATIONAL: the service economy (no line of supply behind it)[1].text
text: What {institution} offers, {settlement} has. It is not a trade with a road attached.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-5.pools.OPERATIONAL: the service economy (no line of supply behind it)[2].text
text: Some of what this town earns has no cargo at all. {institution} answers people, and people come.

DS-SUP-1: Supply › SupplyChainsPanel node graph · `activeChains[]{resource, resourceDepleted, upstreamMissing[], processingInstitutions[], outputs[], exportable, entrepot, upstreamNote}` × roster presence
The line from {resource} to {good} is unbroken: the workings feed {institution}, {institution} finishes the work, and the finished goods leave the town as trade.
Follow {resource} through {settlement} and it does not stop anywhere. It goes into {institution} raw and comes out of the gates as {good}.
This is the trade the town is known for. Every hand in the line between the {resource} and the road is one of {settlement}'s own.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-SUP-1.pools.A PROCESSING HOUSE MISSING FROM THE ROSTER[0].text
text: {settlement} has the {resource} and not the {institution}. The line ends where the working should begin, and the raw goods go out raw or not at all.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-SUP-1.pools.A PROCESSING HOUSE MISSING FROM THE ROSTER[1].text
text: A stranger looking for {institution} here will not find one. What the town takes out of the ground, it sends on for somebody else to finish.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-SUP-1.pools.A PROCESSING HOUSE MISSING FROM THE ROSTER[2].text
text: The step that would make {resource} into {good} is not here. It has to be sent for, or done without.
{settlement} does not raise the {resource} its {chain} runs on. It buys it, and the line works exactly as long as the buying does.
The {chain} is whole on the town's side and borrowed on the far side; {institution} has everything it needs except the beginning of the line.
What goes into the {chain} comes from elsewhere. The work is local; the material is not.
The {resource} is worked out. The line above {institution} is still drawn on the rolls and there is nothing coming down it.
‹needs a dated depletion› {settlement}'s {resource} gave out {timeband_since} and the town has not found another. The workings are still there; what was in them is not.
What {institution} still works, it works on what is left. The {resource} is exhausted and the line is running down the last of it.
Nothing in this {chain} begins or ends here. Goods arrive finished, are counted, and go on, and the town's return is on the counting.
A stranger tracing {good} through {settlement} finds no workshop in the line at all: only a yard, a clerk, and the next road.
The town does not make it and does not use it. The town moves it.
The {chain} is on the rolls and off the road. There is no way to move what it makes, so it is not being made.
The workings above {settlement} sit idle. It is not that there is nothing in them; it is that nothing can be got away from them.
The town has the {resource} and no use for it. Without a road out, the ground might as well be empty.
DS-ECO-6: Economics › Shadow economy · `economicState.safetyProfile{blackMarketCapture, economicDragDesc, criminalInstitutions[], crimeTypes[]}` + `activeChains[needKey==='criminal_economy']`

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-6.pools.TIER: a large share off the books (≥30)[0].text
text: A large share of what {settlement} earns never reaches a ledger. The duties collected fall well short of the trade actually done, and the gap is not an accounting error.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-6.pools.TIER: a large share off the books (≥30)[1].text
text: Half the business of this town is done in the ordinary way and the rest is done quietly. The quiet half is not hiding especially hard.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-6.pools.TIER: a large share off the books (≥30)[2].text
text: A stranger who trades honestly here will be undersold and will not immediately understand why. {faction} is not paying what he is paying.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-6.pools.TIER: a large share off the books (≥30)[3].text
text: The guilds are losing their grip a little further each season. Anyone can undercut a guild price by simply not being in the guild.
Significant off-book activity. Merchants operating in the shadow economy have a cost advantage over those paying duties and guild fees.
A real portion of {settlement}'s trade sits outside the rolls, enough that the men who do pay their duties are competing at a disadvantage.
There is a cheaper way to do most things here, and most people know somebody who knows it.
The prices in this market do not quite add up for a stranger who assumes everyone is paying the same fees. They are not.
Minor shadow activity. Petty theft and small-scale unlicensed trade. An inconvenience, not a structural threat.
A little of {settlement}'s trade goes unrecorded, small enough to annoy the clerks and too small to change what the town is.
There is some thieving and some selling without a licence. Every town this size has both.
What passes for a shadow economy here has never grown into one. There is unlicensed trade and nothing organised behind it.
DS-ECO-7: Economics/Services › Economy freshness note · `reconciliationLog[]` walked to the last `regenerate` boundary × `variant ∈ {tallies, catalog}`
Events recorded after this settlement's last survey may not be fully counted in these tallies yet.
The counts on this page were taken at the last full survey of {settlement}. Anything recorded since then may not have reached them yet.
These figures describe {settlement} as it was judged at its last survey. Events entered after that judgement may not be counted in them yet.
What follows is the last careful reckoning of {settlement}, and it may not be today's.
Events recorded after this settlement's last survey may not be fully counted in this catalog yet.
This list of what {settlement} offers was drawn at the last survey. A house opened or closed since then may not appear on it yet.
The catalog describes the services {settlement} was judged to hold. Later changes may not be counted in it yet.
What the town could do for a visitor was written down at the last survey, and may have moved since.
{settlement} eats what it raises and keeps almost nothing back. A year here is measured by whether it was got through.
There is no spare anything in this town: no spare grain, no spare coin, no spare hands. What it has is what it is using.
The accounts run to survival and stop. Nothing is set aside because there is nothing to set aside.
{settlement} is short more often than not. Some needs are met and some are postponed, and which is which changes month to month.
The books never quite close. What the town needs and what the town has are near enough to argue about and never near enough to settle.
A stranger sees the shortage in the small things: a repair not made, a stall not restocked, a hall not heated.
{settlement} covers what it must and nothing beyond. Every essential is accounted for and there is no line for anything else.
The town gets by. Nobody is going without bread and nobody is building anything either.
{settlement} looks maintained rather than made. What stands is kept standing; nothing new goes up.
The accounts come out steady with a narrow margin. It is an ordinary town's arithmetic and it works.
Things are fine. Not comfortable, not tight: fine, and fine is what people here expect.
Nothing about {settlement}'s condition asks to be remarked on. The town supports itself and has a little in hand.
{settlement} runs a reliable surplus. The margin is not large and it is dependable, and there are reserves behind it.
People here put things by, and can. That is the difference between this town and a poorer one.
The town is plainly past subsistence. The buildings are finished rather than patched, and the stores are more than the season needs.
The surplus is large enough to be spent rather than merely held, and the spending shows in what the town keeps up.
{settlement} is visibly well off. The halls, the walls and the roads are all better than a town this size strictly requires.
There is money here and it goes into the town. Nobody argues about whether a thing can be afforded, only about whether it should be done.
{settlement} holds reserves deep enough to sit out most of what could happen to it. The accounts are not merely positive; they are cushioned.
The wealth here is not the kind a stranger has to look for. It is in the scale of everything at once: the gates, the halls, the goods on ordinary stalls.
The town is rich and behaves like it. What would be a crisis elsewhere is an expense here.

DS-ECO-9: LADDER › food security + the food ledger + the siege interaction · `economicState.foodSecurity` (6 rungs) + `foodLedger(){resilienceScore, storageMonths, deficitPct}` + `stockpile.{blockaded, blockadeBypass}`
{settlement} raises well past what it eats. The excess is stored against a bad season and, in a good stretch, sold.
Food is the least of it here. The fields have been generous and the stores can take a failure without anyone going short.
A stranger will be fed generously and will not be thanked for noticing. There is more than enough and it is unremarkable to anyone local.
{settlement} feeds itself with a small margin. The counts come out ahead by a little, every season, without much drama.
The town eats. It is not a subject anyone raises unprompted.
{settlement} is fed and only just comfortably. The margin is real and thin enough that a good season and a poor one feel different.
The food counts come up short by a little, and the little has to be found somewhere every season.
There is enough, mostly. People here have started noticing the word "mostly".
{settlement} is not hungry and has no cushion. A shock to the fields or the road would be felt inside a season.
A substantial part of what {settlement} eats is bought rather than grown. The town's food is a trade item, and the trade is not optional.
The carts feed this town as much as the fields do. Everybody knows what day they come and what it means if they do not.
{settlement} is fed and dependent. Nothing about the arrangement is failing; everything about it rests on the road staying open.
{settlement} cannot feed itself and does not come close. The shortfall is large, standing, and covered incompletely.
There is not enough here and there has not been for a while. What comes in helps and does not close the gap.
What the town raises falls far short of what it needs, and the difference is being taken out of the stores rather than made up from anywhere.
There is not enough food in {settlement} and no arrangement is bringing enough. The counts have stopped being a margin and started being a total.
The town is hungry. Not short, not pressed: hungry, and the ordinary answers have already been tried.
A stranger is not fed here now. Whatever {settlement} has left is not being offered to anyone who does not belong to it.
The stores are sealed off from the road. What is inside the walls is what the town has, and no count is being added to it.
Nothing is coming in. The granary is the whole of the argument now and everybody is doing the same arithmetic.
{settlement} is cut off from its supply and eating down what it holds. The stores are answering the siege in place of the fields.
{settlement} is cut off and is still being fed. Something is getting past the line, not much of it, and enough to keep the counts from collapsing.
The stores are falling more slowly than a closed road should allow. A way in is still open and it is not on the returns.
The town is meant to be shut and the market is not empty. Nobody local will explain that, and everybody local has noticed it.

DS-SUP-2: LADDER › canonical supply-chain status + the break-cause clause library · `deriveSupplyChainState(chain, settlement)` → `{status, upstreamNote, magicNote, magicRecovery, resourceCondition, dependency, regionalPressures[], substituteActive}` + `supplyShipments{severingCause, weeksCut}`
The line holds. Every input the {chain} needs is present, and nothing in it is being covered for.
The {chain} works. There is no story in it this season.
Nothing about {settlement}'s {chain} draws attention, which, in a line of supply, means all of it is arriving.
The {chain} is meeting its needs and meeting them exactly. There is no slack anywhere in the line.
The {chain} runs under weight. It has not failed and it has nothing left to absorb a failure with.
The people working the {chain} are keeping up. Keeping up is all they are doing.
The {chain} is producing below what it should. The line is intact and the volume coming off it is not.
The workshops on this line are open and half-busy. What they turn out is short of what they are built to turn out.
Output is falling away rather than stopping. Each turn takes a little more off what the line delivers.
The {chain} is off. Something above it failed hard enough that nothing reaches the line at all.
The {chain} is not running. Not slowly. Not at all.
A stranger will find {institution} shut and the yard behind it empty. Whatever fed this place stopped feeding it.
The {chain} still runs and no longer runs for the town. {faction} takes its cut at the point everything must pass, and the cut is an arrangement rather than a theft.
Everything on the {chain} goes through the same hands now, and those hands are paid before anyone else is.
The {chain} looks ordinary from outside {settlement}. Inside it, one name sits on every stage.
The {chain} runs on something other than its own supply. The output is real; the line beneath it is not the line that should be there.
What holds the {chain} up is a working, not a road. Take the working away and the line is what it actually is.
The {chain} keeps producing and nobody local mistakes that for health.
The {chain} is failing from several directions at once. No single break explains it and none of them are being answered.
The {chain} is coming apart rather than stopping. Each pressure makes the next bite harder, and the line shortens as it goes.
People are leaving the {chain}'s trades. That is usually the last thing that happens, not the first.
DS-ECO-10: LADDER › export posture, market scarcity, and the freshness caveat · `deriveExportPosture(settlement){status, exports, count, isEntrepot, access}` + `commodityBandForGood(...)`
{settlement} sells nothing outward. What the town makes, the town uses, and the accounts have no export column at all.
Nothing leaves here for trade. A stranger looking to buy in quantity has come to the wrong town.
There is no trade out. Whatever surplus there is stays, and is eaten or worn here.
{settlement} exports one thing. The whole of the town's outward trade rests on {good} and there is nothing behind it.
The outward trade is single-stranded: {good} goes out, and if {good} stops the column is empty.
Ask what this town sells and you get one answer, given without hesitation and without a second item.
{settlement} has goods to sell and no dependable way to move them. The exports are real and the road they leave by is not.
What the town makes has to get out over the {access}, and the {access} is not the kind of road a trader counts on.
The trade exists at the sufferance of the approaches. Nothing is wrong with the goods; everything is uncertain about the going.
{settlement} sells on what it never made. The export column is full of goods that entered the town as imports the same season.
The trade here is in the moving of things. Very little of what leaves began here.
The town's living is the road. Goods come, goods go, and the town takes its part of both.
{settlement} buys more than it sells, and the imbalance is structural rather than seasonal. What the town needs, the town does not make.
More arrives here than leaves. That is simply how the town is arranged and everyone trades around it.
The outward trade does not cover the inward. It works while there is something to pay with.
{settlement} sells several things outward and depends on none of them alone. The export column is broad enough to lose a line without losing the trade.
The yards here are full of goods bound out and no two of them are the same. This is a town that sells.
There is always something going out. If one trade is quiet, another is not.
The stores of {good} are well under what the market keeps, and the reckoning has climbed accordingly.
There is little {good} to be had here, and it costs what little things cost.
A stranger wanting {good} in {settlement} will find it and will pay for the finding.
{good} sits at its accustomed level in the stores, and its price sits with it.
{good} costs what {good} costs. There is nothing to say about it.
The market holds {good} in the ordinary quantity at the ordinary price.
{settlement} holds more {good} than it keeps room for, and the reckoning has come down under the weight of it.
There is {good} everywhere in this market, and it is going cheap because there is {good} everywhere.
A stranger stocking {good} does well here. The town has more than it can use.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-10.pools.THE FRESHNESS CAVEAT: for any surface printing a derived tally[0].text
text: The tallies below are the last survey's. They describe what {settlement} was judged to hold and may not carry what has happened since.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-10.pools.THE FRESHNESS CAVEAT: for any surface printing a derived tally[1].text
text: These counts stand as the town's own last reckoning of itself, and a later change may not be in them yet.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_ECONOMY.DS-ECO-10.pools.THE FRESHNESS CAVEAT: for any surface printing a derived tally[2].text
text: What is written here was true at the survey. Nobody has recounted it.

DS-ECO-11: Resources/Overview › Terrain identity, economic strengths, and the exploitation ladder · `resourceAnalysis.{terrain, strategicValue, economicStrengths[], exploitation{unexploited[], partiallyExploited[], fullyExploited[]}}`
{settlement} keeps its back to the land and its face to the water, and everything the town is good at begins at the tideline.
The ground here gives less than the water does; what {settlement} counts as its own produce comes off boats more often than out of fields.
The weather that matters in this town is the weather out at sea, and everybody watches it whether or not they sail.
{settlement} sits on ground that grows things without argument, and the town's whole arrangement follows from that one fact.
The country around {settlement} is open in every direction: good for a plough, good for a cart, and good for anything else that wants to reach the town.
There is nothing between this town and the horizon but what the town has planted, and the town knows both halves of that.
The timber and what lives in it are {settlement}'s standing wealth; the fields here are clearings rather than country.
The trees come nearly to the doorframes at {settlement}, and the town has arranged its light, its roads and its watch around them.
Everything in this town is made of what grows around it, and the making is the trade.
{settlement} works ground that rises: small fields, hard carting, and whatever the slopes hold that the flat land does not.
Nothing at {settlement} is level, and the town has made a virtue of it. The approaches are slow and the sightlines are long.
The work here is uphill in the literal sense, and the town prices its carting accordingly.
What {settlement} lives on comes out of the rock rather than off the ground, and the season is short at both ends.
The town sits in a place that had to be argued for: high, cold, and holding something worth the height.
Everything this town does not dig out of the mountain, it carries up to itself.
The water is {settlement}'s road and its mill both, and the town's earnings divide along it rather than around it.
{settlement} is arranged lengthwise on its water, and a stranger meets the town by walking upstream or down.
The river decides what this town can move and when, and nobody here treats that as a hardship.
{settlement} exists where it does because of water rather than soil; the ground gives almost nothing and the town's whole economy is arrangement.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_POWER.DS-POW-7.pools.consolidation 0: a fully divided court (live layer, no ruling bloc)[0].text
text: No combination at {settlement} holds enough of the hall to govern it; every decision must be assembled separately, and several are not assembled at all.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_POWER.DS-POW-7.pools.consolidation 0: a fully divided court (live layer, no ruling bloc)[1].text
text: The court at {settlement} is divided finely enough that it is cheap to influence. A small interest buys a great deal here, because there is no majority for it to have to outbid.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_POWER.DS-POW-7.pools.consolidation 0: a fully divided court (live layer, no ruling bloc)[2].text
text: The town waits longer for answers than a town this size should, and the waiting is arithmetic rather than idleness.
A working majority sits at {settlement} with the {seat} inside it; what the hall decides is decided by that combination and announced by the {seat}.
The town knows which houses go together at {settlement} and takes its business to whichever of them is nearest.
There are interests at {settlement} outside the governing combination with real weight, and they do not move. Outbidding a settled majority costs more than any single question is worth.
What holds the combination at {settlement} together is a trade: seats and revenue for a working majority, seat-held rather than personal, and outbiddable by anybody who arrives with more.
The arrangement in the hall at {settlement} is a business one and is treated as one by everybody in it.
The majority at {settlement} survives every leader it has and would not survive a better offer, and there is no secret about which risk it is running.
The combination at {settlement} is held by a personal loyalty between the people at the head of it, strong while those hands hold those seats, and worth nothing the moment either changes.
The alliance in the hall at {settlement} is between two people rather than two houses, and the town has noticed which.
What binds the majority at {settlement} will die with its bearers' tenure rather than with the arrangement, and the succession that ends it has not yet been called.
The seats that hold together at {settlement} hold together on a shared creed; it is the most durable binding in the hall and the least negotiable.
The houses that agree at {settlement} agree about something larger than the town, which makes them very hard to divide over anything smaller.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_POWER.DS-POW-7.pools.glue threat (a common danger at the walls)[0].text
text: The fractious have closed ranks at {settlement} because of what is at the walls; the combination is real, effective and entirely contingent on the danger continuing.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_POWER.DS-POW-7.pools.glue threat (a common danger at the walls)[1].text
text: What holds the hall at {settlement} together is outside it, and will leave when the danger does.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_POWER.DS-POW-7.pools.glue threat (a common danger at the walls)[2].angle
DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_POWER.DS-POW-7.pools.glue threat (a common danger at the walls)[2].text
text: Houses at {settlement} that have not agreed on anything in years are agreeing now, and none of them mistakes it for a reconciliation.

One of the seats in the combination at {settlement} carries a leash, and the combination does not name it aloud. It is the strongest binding in the hall and the only one that shatters rather than loosens.
What holds the majority at {settlement} together would end it in a single afternoon if it were said out loud, and everybody inside it is arranging their affairs accordingly.
The hall at {settlement} agrees on more than it should and nobody outside it can account for why.
What the combination at {settlement} wants is office. Everything else it takes up is taken up for the effect on who holds what.
The combination at {settlement} takes an interest in everything and cares about one thing, and the one thing is who is sitting where.
What the combination at {settlement} is assembling toward is a hall it does not have to assemble anything for, and each season's trade moves it a little nearer.
The combination at {settlement} is organized around money, and its politics are legible the moment the question is framed as a cost.
The houses that agree at {settlement} agree about money, and the agreement lasts exactly as far as the money does.
A stranger who wants something from the combination at {settlement} is not asked what he believes, only what he is offering.
The combination at {settlement} is organized around a belief and will spend office to serve it, which its rivals consistently fail to price correctly.
The combination at {settlement} will not trade the thing it is about, which its rivals keep discovering after they have made the offer.
There are seats the combination at {settlement} could take and will not, because taking them would mean conceding the point the combination exists to hold.
The combination at {settlement} has one purpose and it is getting the town through; anything not bearing on that is being deferred and openly so.
Everything the combination at {settlement} is doing is aimed at the town still being here afterwards, and it says so plainly.
The combination at {settlement} is spending its own future to buy the town a present one, and every member of it knows the bill is coming.
What the combination at {settlement} serves is somebody's interest rather than the town's, and the somebody is not always in the town.
The combination at {settlement} serves an interest, and the interest is not a faction of this town and is not always in it.
What the combination at {settlement} pursues answers to somebody who never appears in the hall, and the answering is the whole of its consistency.
Houses at {settlement} that had no arrangement now have one, and the hall's arithmetic changed the day they announced it.
Two interests at {settlement} started voting together and have not stopped, and the town worked out what that meant before the hall admitted it.
A stranger who dealt with {settlement}'s hall before the season finds two houses now answering as one, and finds nobody willing to explain when that started.
The combination at {settlement} is not the combination it was; a seat left and another took its place, and what the majority wants moved with it.
The alignment at {settlement} has shifted rather than broken, and what it will now agree to is a different list from last season's.
The combination at {settlement} kept its name and changed its mind, and the town noticed the second before it noticed the first.
The combination at {settlement} has come apart. It lost its members and dissolved, and the hall is back to assembling each decision separately.
The arrangement in the hall at {settlement} ended, and it ended over a burden that fell on one house and not the others. That house is the aggrieved party now, and says so.
A leader who bound the combination at {settlement} left the seat and the personal loyalty went with them; nothing seat-held remained to hold the rest together.
The leash was dragged into the light at {settlement} and the combination shattered in scandal; what had been the hall's most durable arrangement was its most brittle.
Something was uncovered at {settlement} and the hall reorganized itself within the week, and the town has a fairly accurate idea of what.

p: DOSSIER_STATE_PROSE_POWER.DS-POW-7.pools.receipt deferred (the alignment exists and has not happened)[0].text
