A major port requires ocean or deep-water coastal access.
A river settlement can have docks but not a major seaport.
A navy requires ocean access. River communities can have patrol boats, not a navy.
Dock facilities require navigable water: ocean coast or navigable river.
A fishmonger requires access to fresh fish: coastal, river, or trade route supply.
Secretly negotiating surrender terms with the besieging force, without the council's knowledge
Treason. The garrison would execute them on the spot if they found out
Has been rationing their own private food stores while publicly enforcing the communal rationing order
The garrison knows about the stores; they've been paid to look the other way
Passed information about the settlement's water supply to someone outside the walls three weeks ago
People have already died because of it; they've been living with that knowledge
Knows a section of the outer wall is structurally compromised and has told no one
Telling the council means explaining why they knew and said nothing for two weeks
Has already made personal arrangements to leave before the final assault. Their family left last week
{npc} saw them loading the cart. They don't know what {npc} understood
The supplies they declared destroyed in a fire are actually hidden in a location only they know
People are starving. The supplies could last another month
Is in contact with the besieging commander (not as a spy, as a former colleague)
The relationship predates the siege. They've been using it to buy time, but the council would not accept the distinction
Authorised an illegal sortie that failed. Five people died and no record was kept
{npc} survived it. They know, and they've been drinking heavily ever since
Has been skimming from the {commodity} reserves to pay a personal debt that predates the siege
The shortage will be noticed when the final accounting is done. They're hoping they die before that happens
Controls a hidden cache of {commodity} reserves that could feed the settlement for two more weeks
{faction} suspects it. They've been watching the property
Sold the settlement's emergency grain reserves three months ago at peak price and reported them destroyed in a flood
The flood was real. The reserves were already gone. The paperwork is missing one date
Has been reporting false harvest figures to the regional authority to suppress aid that would undercut their price control
People have died. The regional inspector arrives in six days
Knows who is hoarding and has made a private arrangement to share the information, for a price
Both the hoarder and {faction} would move against them if either found out
Their family has been eating normally throughout the famine (not from stores, from a private source they will not name)
{npc} has noticed. They asked once. They were told to forget it
Helped engineer the original supply disruption that triggered the famine, believing it would only last a week
It has lasted six. They did not anticipate this. They cannot undo it. They cannot admit it
Is receiving {commodity} shipments through a covert route and selling them at triple the official price after dark
Three people know. One of them is already dead. The other two don't know about each other
Has documentation proving the famine was caused by export decisions made by {faction}, and has been paid to lose it
The documentation exists in another form. Somewhere
Has been feeding information to the occupation authority since the first week, not under duress
{npc} is part of the resistance. They trust this person completely
Made a private arrangement with the occupation commander that ensures their safety and their family's at the cost of three others' names
Those three people don't know why they were arrested
Was part of the original resistance but surrendered their entire cell's identities to avoid imprisonment
Some of them are still alive in the occupation's custody. They believe they were betrayed by someone else
Has been documenting occupation atrocities in secret, but for sale to the highest bidder, not for justice
{faction} would pay well. So would the occupation authority, to suppress it
Their position under the occupation exists because they helped legitimise the takeover (a public statement they made in the first week)
They were told it was just paperwork. They knew it wasn't
Is smuggling people out, but only those who can pay, and the price has been rising
{npc} can't pay. They've been waiting for weeks. The next group leaves in two days
Knows the occupation commander's real orders (not the stated ones), and those orders include a date
The date is soon. Telling anyone means explaining how they know
Has been playing both factions simultaneously, feeding each the other's plans
{faction} just sent someone to verify information that won't check out. The meeting is tomorrow
The vote that split the council was not actually close. They falsified the count
The original tallies still exist somewhere. {npc} was in the room
Has already agreed to support whichever faction wins in exchange for a specific appointment they have not disclosed
They've made this offer to both sides. Both sides believe they have an exclusive commitment
Was responsible for the incident that triggered the fracture: an act of deliberate sabotage they've successfully blamed on the other faction
One member of the faction they framed knows the truth and has been building a case
Knows where the settlement's founding documents are (documents that would legally invalidate the current governing structure entirely)
They've been sitting on this information for eighteen months, waiting for the right moment
Their public neutrality is a cover. They are actively funding one faction's operations through a third party
{npc} traced one payment. They came to ask about it. They accepted the explanation. They didn't believe it
The debt was not authorised by the council. They signed alone under pressure and have been hiding it for two years
{faction} is about to discover this in the accounts they requested
Has been making personal side payments to the creditor's representative in exchange for delay notices that look official
The representative's records will be audited when the contract matures. In three months
Knows the debt contains a clause that transfers significant civic assets to the creditor on default (a clause that was buried in the original document)
{npc} is a notary who helped draft it. They've been avoiding eye contact for six months
Has been embezzling from civic funds to make personal debt payments, using the same creditor network for both
The two debts are about to merge in a way that will be impossible to explain separately
Sold privileged commercial information to a foreign merchant house to cover an interest payment (information that {faction} considers proprietary)
The merchant house used the information publicly. The source will be traced
The original {commodity} contract that created the debt was based on projections they knew were false at the time of signing
The creditor's representative has begun asking questions that suggest they've found the original projection documents
Has already transferred personal assets out of the settlement to a safe location, anticipating default and the personal liability that follows
{npc} helped with the transfer. They've said nothing. They're waiting to see what they get for their silence
They were the betrayer, not the person the investigation has been pursuing
The evidence against the other person is circumstantial but strong. Letting it proceed is the easiest thing in the world
Knows who did it and has said nothing. The betrayer is someone they owe a significant debt to
The debt is called in if they speak. The settlement suffers if they don't. They've been choosing themselves for six weeks
Participated in the original betrayal in a minor capacity and has been helping frame someone else ever since
{npc} saw them at a meeting they claimed not to attend. {npc} has not yet understood what they saw
Has the actual evidence of who committed the betrayal. They found it accidentally and immediately hid it
The evidence also implicates {faction}, which means the fallout would be much larger than anyone currently expects
Was approached before the betrayal and said no, but also said nothing to warn anyone, for reasons they still believe were defensible
If the investigation reaches them, the question of what they knew and when will end their career even if they're not charged
Has been meeting with someone whose affiliation they now suspect. They didn't know at the time, and stopping the meetings would confirm they suspect something
The information passed was minor. Or seemed minor. They're no longer certain
Noticed an inconsistency in {npc}'s behaviour three weeks ago and said nothing, deciding it was probably nothing
It was not nothing. And now they've waited too long to raise it without explaining why they waited
Their correspondence has been read (by whom, they don't know), but the evidence is there for anyone paying attention
The correspondence contains something that would end their career if taken out of context. It will be taken out of context
Is the infiltrator, placed by an outside interest before the settlement's current leadership took power
Their handler has not made contact in four months. They don't know if that means the operation is over or if something has changed
Was recruited by the infiltrating party a year ago and has been passing low-level information, telling themselves it doesn't matter
They were recently asked for something that does matter. They said yes
Knows the disease's origin and has been suppressing that information to protect someone they care about
The outbreak has spread to three more households since they made that decision
Has already been exposed and is symptomatic, presenting publicly as unaffected
{npc} stands close to them every day. They've said nothing
The quarantine order they're enforcing doesn't apply to shipments from a specific merchant they have a financial relationship with
That merchant's last shipment arrived four days ago
Has been selling access to unquarantined routes for cash. The price goes up as the desperation increases
Three of the people who paid are now symptomatic. They know where they got through
Falsified the initial case count to prevent panic, and now the actual count is far higher than the official record
{faction} is about to do their own independent count as part of a resource audit
Is hoarding medicinal {commodity} that should have been distributed, rationing it for their own use and close associates
The official stores are now visibly insufficient. Someone will investigate where the gap is
Has already committed to supporting a specific claimant in private, while publicly presenting as neutral
They made the same commitment to the other claimant last week
Knows the deceased's actual wishes regarding succession. They were told privately and have chosen not to share them
The wishes favour neither of the current claimants. Sharing them would destabilise everything and serve justice simultaneously
Has a document that would legally resolve the succession, in a direction that would require them to give up their current position
They've been sitting on it for three weeks. The longer they wait, the harder the explanation
Was promised a specific appointment by one claimant in exchange for a public endorsement they have not yet delivered
The claimant is now asking why the endorsement hasn't come. The answer is that the other claimant offered more
Has been quietly removing records from the archive that would complicate the succession in ways they prefer not to see complicated
{npc} manages the archive and has noticed the gaps. They've raised it with {faction}
The attacks are not random. They sent a patrol into that territory three weeks ago and provoked something. No one came back. They filed a false report
The survivors' families believe their people died in an accident. They've been asking questions
Has been negotiating with the creature threat on their own authority, and the terms they've offered include access rights the settlement doesn't know they gave
{npc} intercepted one communication. They don't fully understand what they read
The {commodity} operation they authorised six months ago disturbed a nesting site. The attacks started three weeks later
The connection is in the geographic data. Someone with the right maps will make it
Has been selling information about patrol schedules to an outside party who claims to be a monster hunter, and may not be
The last three ambushes hit patrols on days that weren't in the standard rotation
Their private property (inherited land outside the walls) is part of the territory being contested. They've been subtly steering the garrison away from it
Two soldiers died in an area they should have been sent to protect
Has been quietly forwarding a share of the taxes they collect to the insurgency (as insurance, not conviction)
If the authority survives, this is treason. If the insurgency wins, it is not enough. They bet on neither side and owe both
Wrote the anonymous manifesto that gave the insurgency its language, and has since publicly condemned it more than once
{npc} recognised the phrasing. They have said nothing, but they read the condemnation with a strange expression
Is the insurgency's contact inside the council, and has been feeding it exactly the information that keeps the fighting away from their own district
Three other districts have suffered. Theirs has not. Someone is beginning to notice the pattern
Ordered a crackdown that killed people who had nothing to do with the insurgency, then falsified the reports to record them as insurgents
The families know their dead were innocent. One of them has kept everything
Has already negotiated their own safe passage with the insurgency's leadership in exchange for opening a gate on a night yet to be named
The night is close. {faction} still believes this person is loyal
Knows the insurgency is being funded from outside the settlement, by a party the authority itself has been quietly dealing with
Exposing the funding exposes the deal. They have been sitting on both halves for months
Has been moving insurgent fighters and sealed messages through the underways (the dug tunnels beneath the settlement), one cellar-mouth at a time
The warren has no map, but {npc} has walked it. If the authority ever forces one, this person's own route becomes the confession
Has been selling residency papers and gate-passes to newcomers who cannot legally settle, at a price that rises with their desperation
The register is falsified in a pattern anyone auditing arrivals would find. An audit has been requested
Diverted the relief meant for the newcomer camp into a private arrangement, and the shortfall is being blamed on the newcomers themselves
People in the camp are dying of the shortfall. The blame is holding, for now
Is themselves a newcomer, arrived a decade ago under a false history that the current upheaval is threatening to expose
The people they would rule against for lying are lying no more than they once did
Has been quietly buying up the emptied properties of those who fled, through a third party, at a fraction of their worth
Some of the departed intend to return. The purchases will not survive their claims, or their questions
Knows the migration was triggered by something upstream (a failed harvest, a war, a purge) that {faction} helped cause and has been concealing
The newcomers carry the proof in their own stories, if anyone here thinks to listen
Signed the order closing the settlement to further arrivals, then made a paid exception for one group now already inside the walls
{npc} was turned away the same week. They saw the paid group admitted. They have not forgotten a face
Has been under-declaring the settlement's stores to the requisition officers and selling the concealed {commodity} to both armies
The next requisition will physically count what the ledgers claim. The ledgers are wrong by a wagon-train
Falsified the conscription rolls to keep their own household's men home, filling the quota with the names of the poor and the friendless
Several of those men are dead. Their families were told it was an honour
Took a private share of the war contracts that made the settlement rich, routed through a merchant house that does not exist on paper
The house's accounts exist somewhere. A rival contractor has been looking for exactly this
Knows the war is going worse than the settlement has been told, and has been quietly moving their family and their wealth ahead of the news
{npc} helped load the last cart. They asked no questions then. They are asking them now
Authorised the seizure of a rival's property as a 'war measure', on evidence they invented
The rival's heir survived the war the seizure was meant to fund, and has come home with the original documents
Has been feeding the enemy's quartermasters the same false supply figures they feed their own, playing both requisitions for the skim
When the war ends, both sides will reconcile their books. The discrepancy points one direction
Converted publicly to the ascendant faith while still practising the old one in private, and has been informing on other secret adherents to prove their sincerity
The people they named trusted them. Some are already ruined. One has not yet been named
Holds the deeds and endowments of the old religious institution, which they were meant to transfer, and has been quietly keeping them in the confusion
Both faiths claim the properties. Only this person knows the documents never actually moved
Engineered the 'miracle' that tipped the settlement toward the new faith, and knows exactly how it was done
The apparatus still exists, hidden. Anyone who found it would unmake the conversion and every career built on it
Was a senior figure in the old faith and surrendered its secrets (its finances, its sanctuary lists, its private sins) to the new one to secure a place
The sanctuary lists named people now being hunted. {npc} was on a list this person handed over
Has been forging records to erase the old faith's marriages, oaths, and legitimacies, retroactively unmaking inheritances and alliances
One of the unmade legitimacies belongs to a family with the means to check the originals
Knows the conversion was arranged for reasons that had nothing to do with faith (a debt, a marriage, a foreign hand) and holds the correspondence that proves it
{faction} would pay to bury it. The other faith would pay more to reveal it
Has been in secret contact with the revolt's leadership, brokering terms the governing faction has refused to authorise
If the negotiation is discovered they hang as a traitor; if it fails the settlement burns. They have told no one
Owned a share of the slave market and has been destroying the records of exactly whom they owned before those records can be turned against them
{npc} kept a copy. They have not yet decided what to do with it
Freed and armed a group of the enslaved themselves, quietly, before the revolt began, for reasons they have not disclosed and cannot now defend
Those they armed are among the revolt's leaders. If it is known who gave them steel, the answer implicates this person entirely
Knows the revolt began because of a specific atrocity the authorities ordered and then denied
The order exists in writing. This person filed it. They have been trying to make it disappear for six days
Has already arranged to flee with their wealth the moment the walls are breached, abandoning the defence they are publicly organising
The garrison is holding partly on faith in this person's leadership. That faith is misplaced
Is protecting one specific enslaved person for private reasons, at the cost of intelligence that would help contain the revolt
The person they are protecting is close to the revolt's leadership. The connection would ruin them if it were traced
Has been running the enslaved out through the underways for weeks before the revolt broke, using smugglers' tunnels no census ever recorded
Those they moved are now among the revolt's fighters, and the tunnel-keepers know exactly who paid for the passage
The settlement is surrounded. Someone in the leadership is considering terms. Someone else is considering a desperate sortie. The players arrive as this decision is being forced.
Land-based economic activity is suspended. Port access (if present) provides a partial lifeline. The only metric that matters is how long food, water, and ammunition hold out.
A grain merchant has food, enough to matter. They will sell it, but their price is not money. The players can intervene in how this plays out.
Short-term economic viability is critically compromised. Normal income projections do not apply.
A resistance cell needs outside help: people who aren't known faces. The occupation's local collaborators include someone the players will recognise.
Revenue flows to the occupying authority. Local institutions continue under oversight.
Something important (a resource, a prisoner, a decision) falls into the contested space between factions. The players can't avoid taking a side.
Decision-making is paralysed. Infrastructure maintenance is being neglected. Crisis is deferred, not resolved.
The creditor has sent a representative to collect (not money, but something specific). Locals are divided between compliance and resistance, and neither option is clean.
A significant portion of revenue is being extracted by the creditor. Capital investment has stopped.
The betrayal had consequences that are still unfolding. The betrayer may still be here. The players know something that could help identify them, or they are the only people who don't have a motive.
Trust in institutions is low. Some key systems are not operating at full capacity as a result.
Something is slightly wrong: a decision that doesn't make sense, a face seen in too many places, a piece of information that reached the wrong hands. The players can notice if they pay attention.
No economic impact yet. The infiltration is strategic, not extractive (so far).

The healer who identified the outbreak first has gone quiet. Their last message suggested the disease is not natural. Accessing them means navigating a quarantine that is not being enforced consistently.
Market activity is reduced. Travel is being discouraged. Some supply chains are disrupted.
Three different factions have approached the players for support, each believing they represent the legitimate or best claim. All three are partly right.
Major decisions are deferred. Some institutions are operating autonomously, for better or worse.

The attacks are following a pattern that suggests coordination, not desperation. Someone is directing this (whether a rival lord, a beast of unusual cunning, or something stranger). The evidence is there for anyone who looks carefully.
Trade disruption is reducing income. Defensive expenditure is increasing. Population anxiety is rising.
The governing faction knows what is happening but cannot admit it publicly without legitimising the insurgency. They need something done that cannot be official.
Tax collection is contested. Several institutions have stopped forwarding revenue to the central authority. Normal governance is functioning on momentum.
The contested religious authority has left a gap in the institutions that depended on it: records, oaths, property, sanctuary. Someone is about to exploit that gap.
Tithing income splits or redirects. Religious market days and fairs are contested or duplicated. Properties of the old institution are in legal ambiguity. Cross-faith trade is complicated.
The revolt's leadership has demands. Some of them are negotiable. The governing faction has not admitted this publicly, and one of them is attempting to open a back channel.
The slave market's commercial operations are suspended. Labour-dependent production is disrupted. The security apparatus is entirely focused on containment.

A crown officer has arrived with requisition orders that will strip the settlement of something it cannot spare. The governing faction must decide whether to comply, negotiate, or find a third option.
Military expenditure dominates the economy. Trade disruption is significant but offset by war contracts for some. Labour shortage from conscription affects agricultural and craft output.
The question is not whether things will change, but who will shape the change and what they will want in return.
Immigration: food balance stressed, labour market disrupted, criminal opportunity elevated. Emigration: tax base shrinking, institutions hollowing, labour shortage emerging.

What the settlement eats, how it stores food, and what it can export
Salt is among the most-traded commodities. Port and crossroads settlements profit from redistribution.
What the earth, forest, and water provide for construction and industry
What craftsmen and guilds produce from raw inputs
Luxury goods are the primary cargo of long-distance trade. Entrepôt cities profit enormously from the markup.
Goods that flow through for redistribution: the wealth of crossroads, ports, and river hubs
Produced in distant lands. Crossroads and port settlements control distribution and take the markup.
Silk is not produced locally at any tier. Port cities control import; crossroads cities control inland distribution.
Entrepôt cities develop banking infrastructure to facilitate large-volume trade. The bank profits from the flow of others.
Ports and crossroads profit by charging for storage, loading, and onward transport, not by producing anything themselves.
Furs originate in frontier/northern settlements and travel south through trading posts. Mid-route settlements profit from the trade.
Wine is produced in specific vineyard regions and consumed everywhere. Port and river settlements profit from redistribution.
What protects the settlement from external threats and internal disorder
What keeps the population alive and attracts pilgrims and the infirm
What the settlement knows, records, teaches, and sells as intelligence
What the settlement can offer in magical services, goods, and infrastructure
Magical items are among the highest-value trade goods. Cities near magical nodes become distribution hubs.
Planar goods are extreme-value entrepôt items. Only metropolis-level settlements can support the infrastructure.
What holds the settlement together: faith, law, administration, and social order
Holy sites generate economic activity through pilgrim spending: effectively a non-trade income stream.
What the settlement does for pleasure, culture, and social release
The shadow economy: what moves without documentation and who profits
Smuggling is the dark entrepôt model. Goods that cannot be taxed or declared flow through criminal infrastructure.

Assess existing thatch condition and plan replacement timing.
Watertight barrels for ale, wine, salted meat, and fish. Essential packaging for trade.
Re-coopering and repair of used barrels. Cheaper than new for small leaks.
Specialty containers: butter churns, water buckets, storage vats.
Dried herbs, tinctures, and simple remedies for common ailments.
Prepared medicines for fever, pain, and infection.
Prepare and inter the dead. Religious rites included where applicable.
Grave markers and carved memorial stones.
Ongoing care of family plots. Purchased in advance.
Dig, inter and close the grave. Rites where there is someone at hand to say them.
A cut fieldstone or a lettered board, made by whoever here can cut or carve.
Keeping a family's row clear of bramble and stock. Settled in labour more often than in coin.
Interment in the parish ground, with the rite that parish keeps.

p: INSTITUTION_SERVICES.Parish burial grounds.Register of the dead.desc
text: The sexton records who lies where. Consulted in inheritance disputes as often as in mourning.
Cut stones and lettered slabs, ordered from the masons who work the churchyard.
A block of ground held by a trade for its members and their households.
Interment outside the gates. The bearers and the cart are found by the ground.

p: INSTITUTION_SERVICES.Burial grounds and charnel house.Lifting and ossuary.desc
text: Bones lifted from filled ground once the term is up and stacked in the charnel house.

p: INSTITUTION_SERVICES.Burial grounds and charnel house.Perpetual plot.desc
text: Ground bought against lifting, held for as long as the endowment holds.

p: INSTITUTION_SERVICES.Burial grounds and charnel house.Memorial inscription.desc
text: Cut stones and lettered slabs, ordered from the masons who work the grounds.
Interment in the ground the ward is assigned to, reached by the burial roads.
Parish rolls copied into one office, because no parish can any longer say where its own dead are.
Ground bought, sold and resold. The revenue office watches the trade, and the trade knows it.
Bearers, mutes and a hired route out through the gate, priced by how much of the city is meant to notice.
Municipal grain reserves. Buffers the settlement against poor harvests.
Daily bread. The staple food of most people. Quality and price vary.
Pies, tarts, and pastries. More expensive, available to those who can afford it.
Bake customers' own dough for a fee. Common where ovens are scarce.
Secure, dry storage for large quantities of trade goods.
Customs-sealed storage for goods awaiting duty payment.
Cool cellars for perishables. Rare but valuable.
Open competitive bidding for goods, property, livestock, and estates.
Liquidate the possessions of a deceased or bankrupt party.
Consign goods for auction. Fee taken from sale price.
The elder hears disputes and suggests resolution. No enforcement, but social pressure is real.
Matters affecting multiple families go to a council of heads. Slow but broadly legitimate.
In good years, small surpluses sold at market. Rare and seasonal.
Control who enters and exits. Levy tolls on goods.
The walls provide refuge for the rural population during raids.
Multiple gated access points. Customs checks and toll collection.
Manned towers and wall walks patrol for threats.
The final defensible point in the city. Holds the essential population if the rest falls.
Command and coordination centre for the city's defense.
The city's primary military asset. Keeps out everything short of a major siege.
City-scale grain storage for siege survival and famine prevention.
Release stored grain to cap prices during shortages.
A brief blessing for travelers on the road. Costs nothing; donations welcomed.
Spoken prayer for safe passage and fair weather.
Small offerings left at the shrine. Accumulated and forwarded to the parish.
Weekly mass. Attendance expected of all residents.
Sacrament of entry into the faith. Required for most civil recognition.
Funeral rites and burial. The church manages the graveyard.
Private confession to the priest. Absolution granted.
Food and a bed for pilgrims and travelers. Free or by donation.
Herbal remedies from the monastic garden for common ailments.
Monks copy manuscripts and documents. Slow but accurate.
Spiritual retreat in the monastery. Silence required.
Distribution of food and aid to the poor on feast days.
High-quality manuscript copying across multiple scriptoria.
Access to unusual texts and scholarly works held by the monasteries.
More advanced divine healing from senior clerics.
Access to venerated relics and shrines for pilgrims.
Buy stolen items at 20-40% of value. No questions asked.
Assess the black-market value of items. Discretion guaranteed.
Connect sellers with specific buyers for higher-value items.
Move stolen goods quietly through a trusted referral network.
Purchase restricted or illegal goods without documentation.
Trade information. This fence hears everything.
Secure hiding place for fugitives. Paid in advance.
Introduction to other outlaws and criminal specialists.
Move illicit proceeds through legitimate-looking commercial activity.
Provide paperwork backing a false business identity.
Ship goods without triggering customs inspection.
Move restricted goods along established smuggling routes.
Get shipments past checkpoints without inspection.
Bring in taxable goods without paying duties.
Move people beneath the walls unseen.
Hold goods in dug caches off the rolls.
Carry cargo with no manifest or toll.
A dug chamber off the passage where someone can wait out a search.
Full criminal marketplace for goods and services unavailable above ground.
Navigate the underground without getting lost or robbed.
Resolve disputes between criminal parties without involving authorities.
Controlled access through the perimeter. Strangers must state business.
Basic patrol of the perimeter after dark.
Refuge for the rural population during raids or attacks.
Levy on goods and travelers passing through the gates.
Check travelers and cargoes for contraband or wanted persons.
Enforce curfew and close gates at nightfall.
Armed escort within the settlement's jurisdiction.
Soldiers available for static guard duty on contract.
An officer witnesses and validates commercial agreements.
Report and recover lost or stolen property.
Signal to neighbouring settlements or the garrison of approaching threats.
Early warning of raiders, armies, or other threats.
Basic divine healing. Closes cuts, reduces fever, eases pain.
Remove contamination from food and water through divine blessing.
Treat common illnesses through divine intervention.
Divine blessing for journeys, battles, or important undertakings.
Identify the properties of magical items and substances.
Advice on magical phenomena, ward design, and arcane questions.
Locate and supply rare spell components.
Scrying service for locating persons or places. Expensive.
Transport people and goods to other permanent circles instantly.
Access to planar destinations via the circle network.
Rapid evacuation via teleportation in emergencies.
The complete range of arcane services from multiple practitioners.
Commission enchantment of items to specification.
Access to district libraries and research facilities.
Dramatic but meaningless predictions. Occasionally accidentally accurate.
Sell talismans and charms of no actual magical value.
Ropes, grapples, torches, pole weapons, and adventuring gear.
Maps of known dungeon complexes. Accuracy varies.
Hire human porters to carry equipment into the dungeon.
Prepared antidotes for common dungeon poisons.
Detailed information on creature weaknesses, habits, and habitats.
Research into historical events, figures, and locations.
Translate ancient, foreign, or obscure languages.
Interpret and explain complex or archaic maps.
Street and square performances: juggling, music, comedy, acrobatics.
Hire the troupe for private events and festivals.
Organize and manage entertainment for a major festival.
Secure, discreet rooms for meetings requiring privacy.
Information gathered from indiscreet clients. Valuable currency.
A place where parties from rival factions can meet quietly.
Hire a private box for exclusive viewing. Status symbol.
Commission or sponsor a production or performer.
Apply for construction, business, and trade permits.
Bring commercial and civil disputes before a magistrate.
Pay annual and quarterly taxes and levies.
File and register contracts, deeds, and official documents.
License all commercial and civic activities in the city.
Appeal decisions of lower magistrates and officials.
Access the city's archive of documents and records.
Official witnessing of commercial and legal contracts.
Short-term detention pending trial or payment of fines.
Stocks and pillory for public shaming and minor offenses.
Pay fines to secure release from detention.
Hold convicted criminals for extended sentences.
Assign prisoners to labour contracts for public works.
Formal hearings to set or deny bail for detained persons.
Obtain a permit to visit an incarcerated person.
Read the day's register of arrivals and what each of them reported.
Bring a rumour you already hold and have it weighed against the register.
Leave a question with the clerk and collect the answer when word comes back.
Ask whether a named traveller passed through, and in whose company.
Commission a written answer on a named subject, graded and sealed.
Search the archive that cross-checks one road's report against another's.
Have a claim graded against every road the exchange keeps.
A patron's regular digest, delivered each season by courier.
Place a paid correspondent on a road the exchange does not yet cover.
Send word by loft, unsigned, ahead of any rider on the road.
Ask a question that no one will remember you having asked.
Where the watch is walking this week, and where it is not.
Find out who a newcomer answers to before you deal with them.
Buy a piece of knowledge with the seller's own grade attached to it.
Commission an answer on a subject that cannot be asked aloud.
Be put in front of the one broker who deals in your subject.
A patron's covert feed, renewed for as long as the payments hold.
Have a story built, laundered through other mouths, and put into circulation.
a custom older than the walls
the day the whole quarter shutters its doors
kept since the first stone was laid
older than any charter the town can show
the one day the roads all lead home
long tables set in the square
shared bread and the common cup
the guild ovens working through the night
a whole ox turned on the spit
the old road walked end to end
drums and the ringing of the bells
candles kept through the dark hours
lantern-boats set adrift on the water
the old names read aloud from the rolls
the roped lists and the champions' ring
the toll-gate thrown open to all
beasts and goods driven in from the hinterland
tithes carried up the temple steps
a garland left at the shrine
In {town}, {name} was set aside this year: hardship left no room for the observance, and a people that keeps its restraint is remembered for it too.{ownerBit}
{name} was set aside in {town} this year; hardship left no room for it, and a people that shows restraint in a hard season is remembered for that too.{ownerBit}
In {town} this year, {name} went unheld: the season left no room for it, and there is a quiet credit in a town that knows when to keep its restraint.{ownerBit}
In {town}, {name} {phrase} this year. A settlement's traditions carry its identity forward; each holding or failing is a mark on the year.{ownerBit}
{name} {phrase} this year in {town}. A town's observances carry its identity forward, and every year they hold or fail leaves its mark.{ownerBit}
This year in {town}, {name} {phrase}. What a people keeps, and how well, is written into the record of the year.{ownerBit}
In {town}, {name} {phrase}. A settlement is known by the customs it keeps; each year's keeping, or failing, is a mark upon it.{ownerBit}
{name} failed badly this year, and the townsfolk are looking for someone to blame: a rich seam of grievance for a party to work.
The failure of {name} has soured the mood in {town}; muttered blame is hardening into factions, and a clever party could tip it either way.
{name} came apart this year. Someone profited from the disgrace, or arranged it. The party may be the ones to find out who.
{town} set aside {name} this year, and the older folk call it an ill omen: a rumour a party could confirm, dispel, or exploit.
For the first time in memory, {name} went unheld in {town}; the quiet has left people uneasy, and uneasy towns hire adventurers.
The setting-aside of {name} has emboldened those who always resented it and alarmed those who need it kept. The party is caught between them.
{name} was a triumph this year, and {town} is thick with visitors, coin, and the cut-purses who follow both: the party arrives at the height of it.
The triumph of {name} has made {town} the envy of its neighbours; someone means to spoil it, and the party may be the only ones who notice in time.
On the strength of {name}'s triumph, a bold claim is being made in {town}. A rival is already moving to answer it.
{name} was traded away under the overlord and now survives only in secret; the party may be asked to help keep it or to stamp it out.
The banned rite of {name} is still kept behind closed doors in {town}, and word of it has reached the wrong ears. The party arrives as the net tightens.
Since {name} was forced under, a quiet resistance has gathered around its memory in {town}. The overlord wants names.
With the occupation ended, {town} keeps {name} openly again for the first time in years. Old scores are being settled under cover of the celebration.
{name} has returned to {town} now the overlord is gone, but the first free keeping stirs up who collaborated and who resisted. The party is in the middle of it.
The restored rite of {name} draws home exiles and grudges alike; {town} has not decided whether it is a reconciliation or a reckoning.
{name}, brought by newcomers, has taken root in {town}, and it chafes against the older custom; the party may be asked to broker, or to take a side.
The settlers' rite of {name} has grown too large for the old families of {town} to ignore, and the friction is turning into something a party could be hired over.
{name} arrived with the newcomers and now rivals the town's own observances; someone in {town} means to see it gone, and someone else to see it crowned.

The five priority sliders (economy, military, magic, religion, and criminal) run from 5 to 95 and default to 50. The engine reads each slider on these five bands to decide how strongly that domain shapes the settlement. The magic slider also resolves to a separate magic level the world reads (see the Magic and Religion tab).
At or below 15. The engine expects almost nothing of this domain; its institutions are unlikely and its mark on the settlement is faint.
Up to 35. A minor emphasis. A few of this domain's institutions may appear, but it does not steer the settlement.
Up to 65. The default weight. This domain carries ordinary influence, neither driving the settlement nor absent from it.
Up to 85. A strong emphasis. The engine expects this domain's institutions to be present and to leave a mark.
Above 85. A dominant priority. This domain's institutions are expected in force and can define the settlement's character.

Every supply chain the settlement runs carries a status shown as a chip on the dossier. These are the states you will see. Two further engine states, captured and collapsing, are defined but not yet produced by the generator.

Not a score. The engine checks whether the settlement makes logical sense and returns one of three verdicts. The findings behind a verdict are graded critical (survival-blocking), implausible (breaks historical believability), dependency (relies on open trade), or inefficiency (waste the settlement can survive).
The pieces fit. The settlement holds together with no survival-blocking problem.
Survivable but strained. It works, yet real weaknesses show.
A critical issue prevents the settlement from surviving as described.
How well the settlement feeds itself, read from local production, imports, and any magical supplement against demand. A famine or a severe deficit caps prosperity no matter how strong the trade.

A food deficit above 40 percent. The settlement cannot feed itself.
Famine. Food has failed outright, and it caps prosperity no matter how strong the trade.

Healthy. Shocks are absorbed without crisis.
Functional but stretched. A bad season would hurt.

Each of the five defense arms (beasts and monsters, invasion and war, internal security, economic survival, disasters and famine) carries a readiness badge on this scale. The settlement's overall defense reads from well defended down to undefended.

At or above 40. Covered, but with little margin.
At or above 20. Thinly covered; a real threat would strain it.

How far the populace accepts the ruling power, on a 0 to 100 scale built from prosperity, safety, defense, and food. It scales how well the ruling power performs and, inversely, how much room crime finds.
At or above 75. The ruling power is broadly accepted; it governs at full strength and crime finds little room.
At or above 60. Accepted, with a modest edge in the ruling power's favour.
At or above 45. The ruling power holds on sufferance, with no edge either way.
At or above 30. Acceptance is fraying; the ruling power weakens and crime gains ground.
Below 30. The ruling power has lost the populace; governance can fracture and crime fills the vacuum.
How far a criminal interest has taken a seat of power.
No criminal capture. The seat answers to its lawful holder.
A criminal interest is pushing at the seat, and the seat is pushing back.
The lawful holder and the criminal interest have reached an uneasy standoff.
The criminal interest now bends the seat to its ends more often than not.
The seat is captured. The criminal interest owns its decisions outright.

A seat is a settlement whose patron is this god. Rank rises with seats (cult to minor at two, minor to major at four) and falls back below them, but a change must hold for two ticks, and at most two ranks change across the whole realm each tick. Rank is earned through spread, so a single custom deity can rise on its own.
A fringe following, with fewer than two settlement seats.
Four or more settlement seats, and only a major god can shift a realm's magic legality.

The authored stance dial (warlike/peacelike/neutral), distinct from the retired `temperamentAxis` mirror, which stays inert forever. W-FAITH F2c landed the read arm: `deityAxes.deityTemper` returns an authored word when one is present (an authored `neutral` wins too) and derives from the alignment axes otherwise. W-FAITH F3c CARRIED THIS KEY INTO THE EMBED (ODQ §866): all four deity-embed writers — deitySnapshotFrom (which is also the restore-from-world path), setPrimaryDeity, imposeCult and reEmbedPrimaryDeity — now copy it through one shared picker, conditionally, so a deity that does not carry the field mints no key and every legacy embed stays byte-identical. The effect is therefore MECHANICAL and measured: the authored word now reaches every embed consumer, and `disposition.computeAggressiveness` moves with it. The boon/bane channel wiring is W-FAITH F4c.

the generation lane mints a brand-new town from the wizard form config on every call; a reroll REPLACES the town rather than re-deriving it, and with a save on screen it explicitly mints a new identity. state.config is never hydrated from a saved settlement, so fullConfig cannot carry an existing world's law. It mints the law here on the main thread and sends it as request data; the executor named below is what actually calls the pipeline.
